checks.json: patch_applies=true; no commands were run, per the experiment setup.

Test dependencies exist in base: generated/tests/test_console.py imports io, sys, pytest (base test_console.py:1-9); generated/tests/test_control.py:2 imports ControlType; generated/tests/test_windows_renderer.py:12 imports ControlType and uses the legacy_term_mock fixture (base test_windows_renderer.py:18-20).
The patch only adds code. The one removed line (segment.py ControlCode union) is replaced by a superset that keeps all prior members.
generated/rich/console.py:1154-1170 defines Console.set_window_title in the Console class, next to show_cursor and set_alt_screen; the reference also places it on Console.
generated/rich/control.py:144-153 defines Control.title alongside the other Control classmethods.
generated/rich/segment.py:52 adds SET_WINDOW_TITLE to ControlType; generated/rich/control.py:33 registers its formatter in CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT.
generated/rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56 adds the Win32 dispatch in legacy_windows_render, the same module as the other control dispatches.
generated/rich/console.py:1154 signature `set_window_title(self, title: str) -> bool`, matching the reference's public name, parameter, and return type.

generated/rich/console.py:1167-1170: returns True after writing the control when self.is_terminal, otherwise False. The reference (reference console.py set_window_title) uses the same gating and does not check legacy_windows.
generated/rich/control.py:144-153: `Control.title(cls, title: str) -> Control` returns cls((ControlType.SET_WINDOW_TITLE, title)), the same construction as the reference.
generated/rich/segment.py:52: `SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16`, the next free enum value, matching the reference.
No new imports were added in any changed source file. console.py already imports Control (generated/rich/console.py:56) and show_cursor already uses it.
generated/rich/_windows_renderer.py reuses the existing `cast`, `Tuple`, and `ControlType` imports (base _windows_renderer.py:1,4).

generated/rich/control.py:33: `ControlType.SET_WINDOW_TITLE: lambda title: f"\x1b]0;{title}\x07"` registers the formatter in CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT. Control.__init__ (base control.py:46-54) dispatches through this map with `*parameters`, so the str parameter is passed through.
generated/rich/segment.py:52 adds the enum member; generated/rich/segment.py:55-60 adds Tuple[ControlType, str] to ControlCode.
generated/rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56 dispatches SET_WINDOW_TITLE to term.set_title(title). LegacyWindowsTerm.set_title exists at base rich/_win32_console.py:534-541.
The patch adds no third-party or new internal dependencies. The only new code is in existing modules and uses existing imports.

generated/rich/console.py:1167-1170 follows the show_cursor pattern (base console.py:1143-1152): an is_terminal guard, then self.control(Control.x(...)), then return True/False. Rendering stays in the Control/Segment pipeline.
The Win32 call is confined to the legacy renderer (generated/rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56), matching the other cursor and erase codes.

The change uses the existing extension points: the ControlType enum, the CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT map, the Control classmethod factory, and the legacy_windows_render dispatch chain (generated/rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56).
No parallel rendering path is added. The console method goes through self.control(...) like its neighbors (console.py:1167-1169 and the reference console.py set_window_title).

Console never calls the Win32 API directly. It emits a Control segment (generated/rich/console.py:1168), and only the renderer translates it to term.set_title (generated/rich/_windows_renderer.py:56).
_win32_console.py:534-541 remains the only Win32 boundary, unchanged by the patch.
Docstrings use the repo's Google style with Args/Returns, like neighboring methods (generated/rich/console.py:1155-1166; generated/rich/control.py:145-152).
CHANGELOG entry sits under [Unreleased] > ### Added, the existing section format (generated/CHANGELOG.md:9-11).

Tests use the repo's existing fixtures and Console(...legacy_windows=False, _environ={}) style (generated/tests/test_console.py:302-307; generated/tests/test_control.py:10-14; generated/tests/test_windows_renderer.py:128-133).

Minor deviation: generated/tests/test_console.py:301-303 adds `skipif(sys.platform == 'win32', reason='legacy Windows renders titles via Win32 API')`. The test passes legacy_windows=False, so the Win32 path is not taken (generated/rich/console.py:1950-1954), and the reason string is misleading. The reference instead uses `if console.legacy_windows: return`. The same skipif + legacy_windows=False pattern appears in base test_console.py:49-61, so this follows an existing convention.

Behavior matches the reference: console.set_window_title writes `\x1b]0;{title}\x07` when is_terminal and returns True; otherwise it writes nothing and returns False (generated/rich/console.py:1167-1170, generated/rich/control.py:33).
Legacy Windows consoles set the title through term.set_title (generated/rich/_windows_renderer.py:54-56).

Shared limitation, not a differentiator: the title is interpolated unescaped into the OSC sequence, so a title containing BEL or ESC would end the sequence early. The reference's CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT lambda has the same behavior.
